newsitem.title: UK: Export data and currency rule Euro vegetable oils.
newsitem.headline: Export data and currency rule Euro vegetable oils.

text.p: Malaysian palm oil export data and the firm dollar ruled the European vegetable oil market on Friday morning.

Data from Malaysian cargo surveyor Societe General de Surveillance (SGS) projected an improved export picture during the first twenty five days of July while the firm dollar could make palm oil more attractive to buyers.
SGS estimated local palm oil exports between July 1 and 25 at 580,916 tonnes against 510,578 tonnes during the same period in June.
In Asia and Europe palm oil prices rallied with crude palm oil cif Europe $5 up at midday after Aug traded at $477.50, Sep at $485 and Oct/Dec at $495 and $497.50 a tonne cif.
Among products RBD palm oil was $2.50 up while olein sellers were unchanged to $2.50 higher after Aug traded at $521.50, Oct at $512.50 and Jan/Mar at $515 a tonne fob Malaysian ports.
Lauric oils were also higher taking their cue from palm oil with coconut oil $7.50 to $5 up and palmkernel oil $5 to $10 higher after Sep/Oct traded at $565 a tonne cif.
Soft oils offers were steady with soy oil 0.50 to one guilder up and rape oil 0.25 to 0.75 guilders higher.
